purpose: Current operational router for archive and collection work. This file supersedes earlier priority snapshots for day-to-day research. It does not alter the frozen surviving-object census.
principle: Prioritize the next source that can close a relation, not the next institution that can add a collection name.

targets.target: Charles Elcock — Whipple + St Andrews correspondence/slides + Challenger/Type Slide lineage
targets.status: S+; commercial product, expedition-material bridge, market reception and distributed survival all documented at series/collection level
targets.closed: Type Slide advertisements/retailers match Whipple TYPE SLIDE No.1/2 drawers; contemporary display and wanted/exchange evidence show public recognition and secondary demand; St Andrews preserves six independent TYPE SLIDE / OSTRACODA examples; Whipple retains a manuscript specimen-list sheet; Heron-Allen/Earland's later Type Slide archive includes some earliest slides marked Charles Elcock. Crucially, St Andrews ms21974-ms21975 are two Elcock letters dated 6–8 March 1884 whose catalogue explicitly notes references to Challenger expedition samples, while Whipple independently preserves Challenger-derived material among Elcock's slides and the 1910 Belfast obituary says Challenger samples were forwarded to him for examination.
targets.next: Request St Andrews ms21974-ms21975 first: they are now the cheapest direct route into who sent Elcock Challenger material and why. In parallel verify the 1882 Type Slide review in BHL and request Whipple 6601.10/6601.11 + drawers 9–12. Only after that transcribe/test the 2024 Flints Challenger cabinet against NHM station data.
targets.payoff: Expedition sample → correspondence → workshop preparation → spatial taxonomic/key system → commercial product → public/secondary market → retained workshop archive → posthumous dispersal.

targets.target: Quekett Microscopical Club + Oxford RMS collections
targets.closed: Cole publication architecture and institutional Library/Cabinet separation are documented; major society slide collections survive.
targets.next: Search existing QMC label transcription for Cole/Martin/Prize Medal/Studies and diagnostic Volume I subjects; query Oxford old slide indexes against a small set of itemised RMS events.
targets.payoff: Published issue/donation event → historical cabinet record → surviving slide.

targets.target: Natural History Museum — H.M.S. Challenger sediment and microscopic-preparation archive
targets.closed: Haeckel's 1887 primary report says John Murray made carmine-stained Canada-balsam preparations on the spot and that Haeckel examined about 1,000 preparations from 168 stations. NHM preserves the sediment/derived-preparation collection, a separate 105-drawer slide cabinet, registration/subnumber layers and an open dataset; named slides include Haeckel-annotated and Norman-prepared examples. Modern CT analysis re-evaluates the material meaning of some historical collecting labels.
targets.next: Download/harvest the NHM resource and subset slide/micro-preparation records. Extract all records naming Haeckel, Norman, Voigt/Hochgesang and other preparators; build station → preparation → publication crosswalks starting with Station 271 and known M-number examples. Use dataset fields to test external Challenger claims such as the Elcock auction cabinet.
targets.payoff: Station/depth/method → shipboard preparation → specialist publication → Edinburgh custody → museum registration/cabinet → dataset → CT reinterpretation.

targets.target: University of Tokyo Medical Library — Anatomy Department nos. 110, 118–123
targets.closed: Course diary, preparation quantity ledger, manufactured histology/embryology catalogue, microscope/instrument index and practical microscopy records are identified as a coherent 1870s–1880s sequence.
targets.next: Acquire page images with covers and original order; extract columns/numbering first; then test preparation categories across production, instrument and teaching records.
targets.payoff: Potential independent paper on institutional production of practical microscopy in Meiji Japan.

targets.target: Cambridge Museum of Zoology / Whipple — Balfour objectives, serial sections and microtome
targets.status: S+ route; publication captions can potentially date instrument acquisition
targets.closed: Balfour embryological sections survive; Whipple preserves a Balfour objective set with Zeiss/Gundlach designations and serial/engraved numbers; the museum states that acquisition dates for some lenses can be traced through plate-caption mentions. A pre-1880 Rudolf Jung sliding microtome from Zoology is the type Foster and Balfour described as the microtome they were most accustomed to.
targets.next: Extract every objective/magnification reference from Balfour plate captions before broad archive requests. Crosswalk those printed references to objective markings, then taxon/stage and surviving slide-series candidates. Treat 1882 F.M.B. engravings as potentially commemorative.
targets.payoff: Objective address → dated plate caption → anatomical preparation/series → surviving section.

targets.target: Harvard Embryological Collection + Charles Sedgwick Minot papers
targets.status: S/A+; rich public crosswalk and strongest seriality-without-publication control
targets.closed: HEC preserves serial sections, original card catalogue, line drawings, previous HEC numbers, current MCZ numbers, technique fields, publication citations and ledger links.
targets.next: Date-filter HEC records to pre-1900 first; sample complete series through old HEC number → card/drawing → technique/preparator → publication → current MCZ number.
targets.payoff: Anatomical seriality is not automatically material publication; HEC is a positive control for relation survival under recataloguing.

targets.target: Stazione Zoologica Anton Dohrn + St Andrews surviving Naples slides
targets.status: S; catalogue/shipment bridge plus surviving external collection
targets.closed: Nine of the twelve June 1880 RMS slides strongly match numbered Naples catalogue offerings. St Andrews independently preserves a named Stazione Zoologica slide group and identifies Fritz Meyer as a major preparer of surviving examples. Delphinus phocaena BPM/1/T8/6 carries manuscript 'Panis 383'; number 383 is structurally plausible inside the derived Mammalia catalogue band, but the catalogue row has not yet been verified.
targets.next: Inspect catalogue row 383 before broadening the Naples search. Then search 1879–1881 preparation-department accounts/copybooks/A. W. Waters correspondence and transcribe St Andrews labels systematically.
targets.payoff: Catalogue → internal order/dispatch → British shipment/use → independently surviving institutional slides, with a possible first object-level catalogue-number closure.

targets.target: Museo de La Plata — Tempère & Peragallo / Möller + Historical Archive
targets.closed: Named historical slide series survive in the same museum that preserves institutional correspondence from 1884 onward.
targets.next: Get current series inventory and label/box photographs first; search acquisition/exchange correspondence by exact names and series numbers.

targets.target: St Andrews Norman + Whipple Wheeler/Watson trade-attribution layer
targets.status: S; catalogue-to-object route expanded into maker/retailer/collector attribution
targets.closed: Norman's 1872 list can be reversed against surviving St Andrews labels, while the Whipple Wheeler 'Planet Mars' slide retains maker mark, Watson retailer label, collector number and current accession.
targets.next: Transcribe physical label layering before catalogue matching; use exact historical subject wording and keep maker, business, retailer and collector namespaces separate.
targets.payoff: Trade history becomes multi-layer attribution rather than a single maker field.

targets.target: Berlese St Andrews subset + Florence CREA main collection
targets.closed: St Andrews preserves 67 similarly mounted COLLEZIONI BERLESE slides in two boxes, with visible numbers spanning 37–194 and Italian localities; the principal Berlese Collection is preserved in Florence.
targets.next: Identify the historical catalogue/key behind the St Andrews numbers, photograph/transcribe all 67 labels and determine the route by which the subset left the main Berlese collection.
targets.payoff: Numbered specialist collection → institutional division → distributed surviving subset.

completed_bounded_harvests.result: Five primary letters establish distinct material relations: preparation for repeat viewing, raw-material consignment, field preservation failure, professional preparator send-on-approval sale, and gift of a Radiolaria glass collection.
completed_bounded_harvests.stop_rule: Reopen only for a named preparator, Radiolaria set, transaction, shipment or surviving collection bridge.
